intro.line: Ravnica: one city that covers a whole world. Ten guilds run it, and ten thousand years ago they signed a contract to share it.
Built on the very ground where the Ten signed the Guildpact, the tower is a monument to the past and a reminder of who holds power in the present.
Nine guilds are famous. The tenth, House Dimir, is a story parents tell. Nobody has ever seen its master.
In secrecy is strength. None can oppose one who cannot be found.

finale.line: Szadek falls in the dark under the city, and House Dimir is a rumour again.
Ten thousand years of contract, and it took a ghost to read the small print.
The Decamillennial is days away. The Guildpact is fraying anyway. Szadek only pulled the first thread.
Everyone knows that violence at the Festival brings the worst of luck, so for at least one day a year arms are laid down in favor of brimming goblets.
On the ten-thousandth anniversary, the Guildpact breaks. The ten guilds are free, and every one of them remembers a grudge.

villainFinale.line: The ghost of Agrus Kos fades into the stone. Teysa's contracts burn.
I am confident that if anyone actually penetrates our facades, even the most perceptive would still be fundamentally unprepared for the truth of House Dimir.
On the Decamillennial, the Guildpact breaks. Nine guilds go to war. The tenth watches, and takes its share, one coin purse at a time.

battles.title: Festival of the Guildpact
battles.blurb: Once a year the guilds lay down their arms for the Festival of the Guildpact. This year a Rakdos cult has come to the party anyway, and the Selesnya Conclave stands in its way.

scene.line: The clamor of the city drowns all voices. But together we can sing a harmony that will resonate from Ravnica's tallest spires to her deepest wells.
Convoke: tap your creatures to help pay for a convoke spell. Each one pays one mana of its colour, or one generic.
The symbol of the Conclave is one of unity, with tree supporting sun and sun feeding tree.

villainScene.line: A Rakdos party is a flop if anyone lives to talk about it.
Great minds bleed alike.

after.line: They came for blood on the one day nobody fights. Something is wrong with the city.

battles.title: The Undercity
battles.blurb: Under Ravnica's streets, the Golgari farm the rot. Their queen Savra has caught Izzet surveyors poking at her gardens with their weird machines.

scene.line: Nature's most raw beauty is the circle: perfect in its continuance, with no break between death and life.
Dredge: instead of drawing, mill that many cards and return the dredge card from your graveyard to your hand. The dead come back to work.
The Golgari don't bury their dead. They plant them.

villainScene.line: Like many Izzet creations, weirds are based on wild contradictions yet somehow manage to work.
Diametrically opposing energies in self-sealed plasmodermic bubbles make great pets!

after.line: When something dies, all things benefit. Well okay, just our things.

hero.win: Back to the soil with you.

battles.title: The Legion's Justice
battles.blurb: Razia's Boros Legion keeps the peace with fire and steel. The Gruul clans want no peace at all, and Borborygmos has sent his raiders into the city to prove it.

scene.line: I do not know which gives me more pride: the legions of soldiers marching in thunderous lockstep, or the cry of the skyknights riding their rocs like jagged lightning overhead.
Bloodthirst: these Gruul creatures enter bigger if you were dealt damage this turn. Block their first hit, and the rest arrive small.
Though less well-known than its army of soldiers, the Boros Legion's mage-priests are as respected by the innocent as they are hated by the ghosts of the guilty.

villainScene.line: Crush them!
The Gruul aren't satisfied with just smashing things. They continue smashing other things with the things they just smashed.

after.line: The Gruul did not plan this raid. Someone told them where our patrols would not be.

battles.title: The Last Honest Cop
battles.blurb: Lieutenant Agrus Kos of the Wojek has thirty years on the force and a body nobody can explain. Every clue points to a guild that is supposed to be a myth.

scene.line: Lieutenant Kos has never met a group of recruits he could not inspire or a mob he could not quell.
We thought we found the victim's clothes lumped in the street. As it turned out, it was the victim, insides sucked out—just a sack of skin and robes.
Transmute: the Dimir pay mana and discard a transmute card to find any card with the same cost. They always have the right tool. Pressure them before they find it.
The first blow is the most important. It often negates the need for a second.

villainScene.line: Dimir rank and file never see nor hear their guildmaster. All orders are given through mysterious necrosages who appear from the shadows, tersely toss out a command, and then melt into the darkness.
In the undercity, forgetfulness is often encouraged at the point of a blade.

after.line: Dimir. The guild that isn't there. My captain laughed at me.
Agrus Kos does not live to finish the case. He comes back to finish it anyway.

hero.half: Hit them before they find it.

battles.title: The Dead Bankers
battles.blurb: Teysa Karlov is an Orzhov advokist: a lawyer for a church run by ghosts. Grand Arbiter Augustin IV of the Azorius has a writ against her family, and he intends to serve it.

scene.line: Piece the tragic notes together and is it not a melody?
Haunt: when a haunt creature dies, exile it haunting another creature. When that creature dies, the effect happens again. In Orzhova, even the dead pay twice.
Unlike most churches, at Orzhova it's best to pray before you arrive.

villainScene.line: As peace should be—gentle yet unstoppable.
Forecast: during my upkeep I reveal a forecast card from my hand and use its effect, and the card stays in my hand for next time.
Azorius military tactics, like their legal tactics, capitalize on delay and nullification.

after.line: The Arbiter was not after my family. He was after a name in our ledgers. A name with no guild.

battles.title: Ghost Dad
battles.blurb: In the real spring of 2006, the Ghost Council of Orzhova anchored a black-white deck players called Ghost Dad. Its worst matchup on paper was Zoo: three colours of cheap beasts and burn.

scene.line: The Golgari raise the bodies of their dead to serve. We raise the spirits of our dead to lead.
Ghost Council drains them and feeds me. Every blocker I trade buys time for the next drain.
Orzhov churches don't pass the plate for collection. They charge for admission.

villainScene.line: At mealtimes, the Gruul customarily omit such niceties as using forks or killing the entrée.
[three colours of teeth]

hero.start: The Council will see you now.

battles.title: Project Kraj
battles.blurb: Momir Vig's Simic Combine grows creatures that pass their strength to each other. Niv-Mizzet, the dragon who runs the Izzet, thinks the Simic stole his research. Both are probably right.

scene.line: The unnatural pressures of life in this city are best withstood by lifeforms that adapt with unnatural swiftness.
Graft: these creatures enter with +1/+1 counters. When another creature arrives, you may move a counter onto it. Spread the strength where it is needed.
Of course it will grow beyond control—it was designed to choose its own evolution.

villainScene.line: Niv-Mizzet's genius and vanity reverberate throughout the mirrored halls of Nivix.
The Izzet learn something from every lesson they teach.

after.line: The dragon kept saying the same thing. The Guildpact is weakening, and someone is helping it along.

battles.title: Szadek
battles.blurb: Szadek, Lord of Secrets, has run House Dimir from the dark for ten thousand years. Agrus Kos, now a ghost bound to Teysa's church, and Teysa herself go under the city to drag him into the light.

scene.line: An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
Being dead has its advantages. He can't kill me twice.
He counters and he waits. Cast your second-best spell first, and save the one that matters for when his mana is tapped.
Guilds often exterminate those who saw or knew too much. Some vindictive souls retain their knowledge, using it in the afterlife to crush the guilded and the vile bargain that gives them power.

villainScene.line: In secrecy is strength. None can oppose one who cannot be found.
Some images are so powerful that one glance burns them into your mind forever. Come, let us gaze on nothingness.
Ten thousand years I have signed their contract in the dark. I will see it torn.

half.line: He is spending his counters. Now, Kos. Now.

battles.title: Solar Flare
battles.blurb: Deep in the archive, a deck that turned a graveyard into a turn-four angel.

archive.format: Standard: Kamigawa block, Ravnica block and Ninth Edition.
archive.what: A three-colour control deck that draws cards with Compulsive Research, discards a big Angel, then brings it back with Zombify.
archive.why: Zombify on turn four put a 5/5 flier that destroys a permanent onto the table long before it could be cast. Wrath of God and Mortify cleaned up the rest.
archive.beat: Pressure early, before the graveyard fills. Keep a creature back after a Wrath of God, and make them use Zombify on a board you can answer.
archive.after: Solar Flare stayed a top deck through 2006, picking up Kokusho and later Coldsnap and Time Spiral cards. Nothing in it was ever banned.

deck.name: Solar Flare
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from 2006 Standard Solar Flare lists, using only Ravnica block and Ninth Edition cards. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: The archive opens on a deck that never wanted to cast its own best cards.
Discard an angel, raise it on turn four. Then I win by turn four.

villainScene.line: The deck does not speak. It digs.

after.line: Recorded: never banned. One of the decks that taught a generation to watch the graveyard.
